messages:
Maya: quick q — thinking about SDK surface for transport fallbacks. do we force a single transport API (sync/async) per language or allow both and have a shim? i'm worried about resume semantics for pagination + retries.
Shaan: i'd vote for the smallest possible surface. shims add a lot of surprising edge cases (esp around idempotency). let languages expose their native iterables but keep a shared contract for tokens.
Eli: agree on small surface, but call out resume token semantics clearly. if a retry happens mid-page, are clients expected to dedupe? need a standard to avoid app-level surprises.
Amanda: also consider streaming vs paginated fetch. e.g. streaming token emission and page-based cursors have different retry models. can we unify with a lightweight "cursor" object?
Shaan: real problem is transport-level retries for generation endpoints. if the transport retries a POST that started generation, server might re-run and duplicate tokens. we either need server-side idempotency ids or client-side dedupe markers.
Maya: proposal: include an optional idempotency_key header per request and a monotonic resume token from the service. transports may retry safely if idempotency_key is present.
Eli: server idempotency is great but isn't always available for every model. fallback: SDK exposes last_ack_token in the cursor. on retry, client resumes from last_ack_token (server should accept resume tokens).
Amanda: SDK ergonomics: python should keep simple generator/iterator, TS should be async iterable, Go should map to a channel or iterator. core contract: tokens are opaque strings + last_ack offset. languages adapt shapes.
CI-bot: test-run: generator-resume tests pending, no failures reported yet.
Shaan: concrete: define a "cursor contract" with fields: token (string), last_ack_offset (int), optional idempotency_key (string). Transport should not swallow server errors; SDK layer decides to retry or fail.
Maya: and add per-route retry policy defaults: e.g., streaming endpoints default to fail-fast, non-streamed paginated endpoints allow conservative retries. document cost/latency tradeoffs and expected duplication semantics.
Eli: tests: simulate mid-stream connection loss + transport retry. assert client sees either duplicate tokens (and can dedupe) or resume from ack. add integration test with a mock model that supports resume tokens.
Amanda: action items: Shaan -> sketch cursor contract + py/ts code examples; Eli -> draft tests and mock harness; Maya -> docs blurb + examples for retry policy.
Shaan: will do, ETA tomorrow EOD.
Maya: perfect, thanks :thumbsup:
